claim: Wat Suwan Khuha (Monkey Cave Temple) sits ~10km south of Phang Nga Town in a limestone cave housing a 15-metre reclining golden Buddha, ancient chedis, and resident macaques; entry is roughly 20 baht and the temple opens 8am-5pm.
quote: The temple is best known for its impressive 15-meter-long reclining golden Buddha. The cave also houses smaller Buddha images and ancient chedis... open daily from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The entrance fee is very low (around 20 Baht).

claim: Visitors are warned that the cave's monkeys snatch sunglasses, water bottles and snacks, and arriving before 9:30am beats the Phang Nga Bay tour buses that pour in 10:30-noon.
quote: the monkeys are known to be curious and quick to snatch unattended items like sunglasses, water bottles, or even snacks... Arrive before 9:30 to have the cave largely to yourself.

claim: Wat Tham Tapan (Heaven and Hell Temple) on the edge of Phang Nga town is entered through an enormous dragon's mouth and contains graphic dioramas of Buddhist hell punishments; admission is free, hours 8:30am-6pm, and not recommended for young children.
quote: the open mouth of a massive dragon sculpture, symbolizing the entrance... The complex specifically depicts Na Rok, the Buddhist hell, populated with disturbing statues in torturous poses... Daily, 8:30 AM to 6:00 PM

claim: Sa Nang Manora Forest Park, a 15-minute drive north of Phang Nga town, has a free 2km nature trail through shaded jungle past cascades, a bat cave and swimmable waterfall pools.
quote: an easy to follow 2km nature trail through the park and it is permitted to swim in the waterfall pools... Entry to the park is free

claim: Takua Pa Old Town's Sunday Walking Street runs along the Sino-Portuguese shophouse strip on Sri Takua Pa Road, serving southern Thai snacks, grilled seafood and sweet roti to a mix of locals and visitors.
quote: Visitors can sample southern Thai snacks, grilled seafood, sweet roti, and fresh fruit... well-preserved Sino-Portuguese architecture, a legacy of its tin mining past.

claim: Takua Pa, originally the spice-trading port of Takola, became a tin-dredging boomtown drawing Chinese, Dutch, Portuguese and British merchants; when tin prices collapsed in the 1900s the foreigners left but the Chinese community stayed and shaped the surviving Sino-Portuguese streetscape.
quote: an important tin dredging area, attracting diverse populations including Chinese migrants and Dutch, Portuguese, and British merchants... tin prices began to fall in the 1900s... While traders departed, the Chinese population remained and integrated into local society.

claim: Thailand ranked among the world's top tin exporters from 1967 to 1984, with Takua Pa's mines a key contributor; the district was renamed after takua, the Thai word for lead, despite tin being the more important ore.
quote: from 1967 to 1984 always ranked among the world's top tin exporters... takua (ตะกั่ว) is the Thai word for lead, even though tin was the most important ore found there.

claim: Koh Panyee is a stilted Muslim fishing village in Phang Nga Bay founded over 200 years ago by Javanese seafarers; about 360 families live there today around a mosque, school, health centre and the famous floating football pitch built by local kids from old fishing rafts.
quote: founded over 200 years ago by a small band of seafaring families from Java, Indonesia... roughly 360 families call the village home... floating football (soccer) field, built by local children from old wood and fishing rafts.

claim: Most visits to Koh Panyee come as a stop on Phang Nga Bay speedboat or longtail tours alongside James Bond Island and Hong Island; modest dress is requested as the village is predominantly Muslim.
quote: guided speedboat tour from Phuket that includes stops at James Bond Island, Hong Island... Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees) and be polite to residents—this is a predominantly Muslim fishing village.

claim: The Moken are an Austronesian sea-nomad people of the Mergui and Surin archipelagos who traditionally lived aboard kabang houseboats; since the 2004 tsunami the Thai government has required the Surin Moken to live in one settlement at Ao Bon on Ko Surin Tai.
quote: Since the tsunami of 2004, the Thai government has mandated that the Moken people of the Surin Islands reside in a single settlement, Ao Bon Bay, on Ko Surin Tai

claim: The Moken's most sacred ritual is the twice-yearly Lobong Ceremony, a community cleansing rite honouring the sea spirits that visitors can sometimes witness during Surin Islands trips.
quote: the Lobong Ceremony, held twice a year. It is the largest and most sacred ceremony of the Moken, symbolizing the cleansing of misfortune, the honoring of the sea

claim: Nam phrik takola, a Phang Nga speciality, is a roasted shrimp-paste relish pounded with kung siap (salt-cured skewered shrimp) and served with boiled and fresh vegetables.
quote: Nam Phrik Takola is a local Phang-Nga speciality, beginning with shrimp paste, roasted until fragrant, pounded in a mortar and pestle with kung siap (salt cured skewered shrimp) then served with boiled and fresh vegetables.

claim: Khao yam is a uniquely southern Thai rice salad of jasmine rice (often dyed blue with butterfly-pea flowers) tossed with toasted coconut, dried shrimp, fresh herbs and pungent budu fermented-fish-sauce dressing.
quote: khao yam is a rice salad tossed with toasted coconut, dried shrimp, herbs, and budu fish sauce... topped with an array of finely julienned fresh herbs, vegetables, and fruits, bound together with nam budu

claim: Southern Thailand's large Muslim population has shaped its breakfast culture around roti served with dal or curry, a direct inheritance from South Indian Muslim traders, and dishes like khao mok gai (turmeric chicken biryani) cooked with dry Indian spices.
quote: Roti canai arrives hot from the griddle, served with a bowl of dal or a golden curry: a direct inheritance from South Indian Muslim traders... Khao mok gai, a favourite of the south's large Muslim community

claim: Long Lae Sunday Market in Takua Thung district is regarded as the area's best non-tourist market — open Sundays 8am-5pm, mostly locals, with ~90% of stalls selling prepared southern Thai food alongside karaoke entertainment.
quote: It opens every Sunday from 08:00 am to 05:00 pm... best non-tourist market in the area... About 90% of the booths offer delicious prepared foods of all types. There are entertainment stages with one being karaoke.
